newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court dismisses case against Enron.
newsitem.headline: Indian court dismisses case against Enron.

text.p: The Bombay High Court on Monday dismissed a petition seeking to stop Enron Corp of the United States from pursuing its Dabhol power project on India's western coast.
"We are greatly happy about the judgement," Sanjay Bhatnagar, vice-of Dabhol Power Company (DPC), Enron's Indian subsidiary, told reporters after the ruling.
"We will concentrate on building the project. Work will resume very shortly," he said.
"Within weeks," he said when asked to be more precise.
Enron has already won more than 20 law suits against its project and the latest appears to be the last opposition to the project, clearing the way for its re-commencement, analysts said.
Judges D.P. Saraf and M.S. Rane of the high court dismissed the petition which had sought the scrapping of Dabhol Power Company's power project because of suspected irregularities.
The petition was filed by the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU).
The full text of the judgement would be released later, court officials said.
Dabhol Power Company is 80 percent owned by Enron Development Corp and 10 percent each by U.S. firms Bechtel and General Electric.
The project, with a gross generating capacity of 2,450 MW, had faced several hurdles after the newly elected government of the western Maharashtra state sought to renegotiate the deal last year.
A new right-wing government, led by the regional Shiv Sena party, launched a review of the Dabhol project and ordered the firm to stop work after coming to office in March 1995.

The main controversy was the price the Maharashtra State Electricity Board would pay Dabhol for the power it would generate. The government renegotiated the deal but opponents said the terms still represented a sell-out to the U.S. firm.
Analysts said there appeared to be no hurdles for the power project with the firm crossing the legal barriers and the state government assuring it of full support.
The first phase of the plant will have a gross generating capacity of 826 MW and should be on line 31 months after construction resumes.
Bhatnagar dismissed talk of large losses run up by Dabhol Power Company after work stopped last year.
"The media has been writing on losses," he said. "All I can say is that our investors, especially banks, are behind us."
